story.asA: As a user sensitive to motion,
story.iWant: I want to minimize animations and transitions in the application,
story.soThat: so that I can use the tool comfortably without discomfort.
story.tasks: - [ ] **Analyze existing UI components for animations/transitions (AC: 1):** - [ ] Identify all animated elements (e.g., loading spinners, navigation transitions, hover effects) in the Next.js frontend. - [ ] Document their current implementation (CSS transitions, JavaScript animations). - [ ] **Implement `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS media query (AC: 1):** - [ ] Apply `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` to existing CSS animations/transitions to disable or simplify them. - [ ] Ensure smooth transitions are replaced with instant changes or fades where appropriate, adhering to accessibility best practices. - [ ] **Integrate JavaScript-based animation control (if applicable) (AC: 1):** - [ ] For JavaScript-driven animations, detect `prefers-reduced-motion` preference using `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`. - [ ] Provide alternative, reduced-motion animation logic or disable animations entirely based on the user's preference. - [ ] **Verify browser compatibility (AC: 1):** - [ ] Test the reduced motion implementation across target browsers (Chrome, Edge, Safari) to ensure consistent behavior and proper application of the preference. - [ ] **Write automated tests for reduced motion (Accessibility Testing) (AC: 1):** - [ ] Create integration tests to verify animations are reduced/disabled when `prefers-reduced-motion` is active. - [ ] Investigate using testing frameworks like Playwright or Cypress to simulate user preferences and assert UI behavior. - [ ] **Update `docs/architecture.md` (CI/CD) (AC: 1):** - [ ] Add a note to the CI/CD section of the `architecture.md` document, highlighting the integration of accessibility testing, specifically for reduced motion, into the automated pipeline.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: * **Given** I have enabled a "reduced motion" setting in my operating system or browser * **When** I interact with the application * **Then** all non-essential animations and transitions are either removed or significantly reduced.

Interactive elements and form submissions on this page may have animations or transitions that need to be adjusted for reduced motion.
Interactive elements, form submissions, and loading indicators on this page may utilize animations or transitions requiring reduced motion treatment.
Any main UI elements or interactive components on the landing page that have animations or transitions will need to be made compatible with reduced motion settings.

constraints.constraint: All non-essential animations and transitions must be either removed or significantly reduced when the user's "reduced motion" setting is enabled.
Implementation should primarily utilize CSS media queries (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`) for CSS-driven animations.
For JavaScript-driven animations, `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` should be used to detect user preference and provide alternative, reduced-motion logic or disable animations.
Browser compatibility testing across Chrome, Edge, and Safari is required to ensure consistent behavior of reduced motion implementation.
Accessibility best practices must be adhered to, ensuring smooth transitions are replaced with instant changes or fades where appropriate.

tests.standards: Unit testing is performed using Jest. Automated integration tests for reduced motion using frameworks like Playwright or Cypress will be implemented. Manual testing will verify animations are reduced/disabled when `prefers-reduced-motion` is active.
